newsitem.title: USA: U.S. West Coast prods notionally unchanged late.
newsitem.headline: U.S. West Coast prods notionally unchanged late.

text.p: U.S. West Coast spot products prices were notionally unchanged late on Tuesday as traders stepped back to evaluate a weekly inventory report.
American Petroleum Institute (API), an oil industry trade group, reported West Coast gasoline stocks fell 302,000 barrels last week, but remained 1.4 million barrels over year-ago levels.
API reported that western refiners saw average capacity rise 2.3 percentage points to 92.6 percent, slightly below the national pace of 94 percent.
Traders said refiners boosted output last week to build stocks ahead of holiday driving and cold weather heating demand.
But this week, West Coast refiners took steps to ease oversupply in the region.
Ultramar shut a California coker for earlier-than-expected repairs and Tosco decided to cut crude runs by 10,000 barrels-per-day, starting Tuesday, traders said.
Spot prices for Los Angeles conventional unleaded gasoline were notional unchanged, with bids 62.50 and offers 63.50 cents a gallon. Premium grade stood five cents above conventional material.
CARB-grade conventional gasoline also went unchanged at 66.50/67.50 cents a gallon. Premium held a 3.5 cents advantage.
Los Angeles offers for low sulphur diesel and jet fuel held at 71 cents, while bids were notionally 70 cents a gallon.
San Francisco conventional gasoline narrowed its discount off L.A. by one cent, after cargoes reportedly left the Bay-area for Florida, brokers said.
